title: Alleged Irish international crime boss charged

The US says Daniel Kinahan is part of a cartel that runs a narcotics trafficking organisation. (Facebook: James English)

The United Arab Emirates has handed over alleged Irish crime gang boss Daniel Kinahan to authorities in Ireland.

Mr Kinahan, who was arrested in Dubai in April, was named as one of three leaders of the Kinahan Organised Crime Group by the US which offered a $US5 million ($7m) reward for the trio's arrest.

Mr Kinahan was charged with directing a criminal organisation at a special court sitting late on Sunday and remanded in custody.

Irish prosecutors have charged alleged Irish crime gang boss Daniel Kinahan with directing a criminal organisation at a special court sitting late on Sunday following his extradition from the United Arab Emirates.

Mr Kinahan, who was arrested in Dubai in April, was named as one of three leaders of the Kinahan Organised Crime Group by the United States in 2022 when it offered a $US5 million  ($7 million) reward for the trio's arrest.

An Irish government plane took flight on Saturday to extradite the suspected transnational cartel boss from Dubai to face trial in Dublin over alleged serious crime offences, local media reported.

Irish media reported that a huge security operation was underway, including armed police, members of the armed forces and the prison service, which recently acquired a bombproof escort van to transport organised crime suspects.

Members of the Garda stand outside the Special Criminal Court where alleged Irish crime gang boss Daniel Kinahan appeared. (Reuters: Natalia Campos)

Irish and British news outlets later reported Mr Kinahan had arrived in Dublin on Sunday evening, local time.

Ireland's Department of Justice declined to comment and Irish Garda police said it would not comment on media reports, adding that Mr Kinahan's case "remains a matter for the authorities in the United Arab Emirates at this time".

Irish Garda police later released a statement to Irish public broadcaster RTE, saying a man in his 40s "was arrested in the United Arab Emirates on foot of an arrest warrant issued by the Irish Courts".

Police in Ireland issued a warrant for Mr Kinahan's arrest for "alleged serious organised crime offences". (Facebook: An Garda Siochana)

The 49-year-old Irishman allegedly ran a group out of Dubai that has been linked by US and European authorities to a vast criminal enterprise dealing in drug smuggling and money laundering.

He was arrested in Dubai in April after a warrant was issued in Ireland for "alleged serious organised crime offences" and lost appeals against extradition.

On arrival in Ireland, Mr Kinahan is expected to be taken to the Special Criminal Court in Dublin amid a large security operation, local broadcaster RTE reported.

People gathered outside the Special Criminal Court on Sunday. (Reuters: Natalia Campos)

According to the BBC, Mr Kinahan is accused of directing activities of a criminal organisation between October 2015 and April 2017.

He was charged with directing a criminal organisation and was remanded in custody.

The transnational group, known as the Kinahan Organised Crime Group (KOCG), is alleged to be the most powerful organised crime outfit in Ireland with wealth estimated by Irish police at over 1 billion euros ($1.6 billion).

Mr Kinahan is expected to appear in Dublin's Special Criminal Court. (Reuters: Lorraine O'Sullivan)

Mr Kinahan would be the second senior figure in the cartel to be extradited from Dubai.

Sean McGovern, described by a judge as a "senior lieutenant in the cartel", was the first senior associate to be extradited after his arrest in 2024.

In June, he was sentenced to 24 years in prison in Ireland after pleading guilty to directing organised crime and attempted murder.

The case related to a long-running violent feud between the Kinahan cartel and the rival Dublin-based Hutch gang.

The US government in 2022 imposed sanctions on Mr Kinahan and other members of his family identified as leaders of the cartel.

The US Treasury alleges that Mr Kinahan was the cartel's kingpin. (AP: Patrick Semansky/file)

It designated them as running a narcotics trafficking organisation active in Ireland, the UK and throughout mainland Europe, and engaging in "money laundering, firearms trafficking, and murder".

The US Treasury said Mr Kinahan was believed to run the cartel's day-to-day operations, while his brother, Christopher, was also designated.

Their father, also named Christopher, aka the Dapper Don, oversaw the gang's property, the US government said, offering up to $US5 million for information leading to the arrest of the father and sons.

Europol also designated the three men as "high-value targets".
